clue.text: Robust, but died after short game

indicators.note: after puts the letter for died behind the cut-down game
short means the word for the game loses its final letter here

parts.note: rugger is a colloquial name for rugby
d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone sturdy who nevertheless collapsed after a brief match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the game; 'after' sets the abbreviation for died at the end. Rugger is British slang for rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugged and robust are synonyms for sturdy, strongly built.

clue.text: Push out of seat, when one tilts?

definitions.text: Push out of seat, when one tilts?

parts.words: Push out of seat, when one tilts?
parts.note: a jouster tilting with a lance aims to knock the opponent from the saddle

explanation.walkthrough: To tilt is to joust; the 'seat' is the saddle, so this is throwing a rider off a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat a mounted rider by force is exactly what jousters tried to do in a tilt.

clue.text: Creator, energy exhausted, introducing Sabbath at last

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

indicators.note: the exhausted word has the picked letter introduced into it

parts.note: dead means exhausted, as in dead on one's feet

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word Sabbath

explanation.surface: A tired God is brought in at the end of the week to rest on the Sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhausted' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies a word for tired; 'introducing' puts the Sabbath's last letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The divine nature itself, the Deity, is the creator in religious language.

clue.text: Hesitation about extremely large jacket

indicators.note: about means the hesitation word goes around the picked letters

parts.note: doubt is hesitation or uncertainty

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of the word large

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over buying an outsize coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters of 'large'; 'about' wraps the hesitation word round them. A doublet is a historical garment, not a modern jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet was a close-fitting man's jacket worn from the 14th to the 17th century.

clue.text: Chap making deal stops short it has strings attached

parts.note: man is a chap or fellow

indicators.note: stops short tells us the word loses its last letter here

parts.note: doling out is dealing out, so making a deal of something is doling

explanation.surface: A man doing a deal breaks off abruptly, as the bargain has conditions attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops short' cuts DOLING to DOLIN; 'strings attached' sounds like conditions but means an instrument's strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandolin is a lute-like musical instrument with paired metal strings.

clue.text: Not believing Greek ambassador is being installed

indicators.note: being installed means the ambassador and is go inside the Greek word

parts.note: Attic means of Athens, so Greek
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faithless Greek envoy is put in post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being installed' puts the ambassador and 'is' inside the word for Greek; Attic is the dialect and region of Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone godless rejects belief in any deity, so is unbelieving.

clue.text: Put out by dialect, so needing translation

indicators.note: translation turns these words into another form, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder as written
fodder as written

explanation.surface: Someone is disconcerted by an accent so thick it must be translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests annoyed, but here it means knocked out of joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislocate a joint is to put it out of place, as with a shoulder.

clue.text: See Hindu goddess in permitted embrace with Eastern twin?

indicators.note: with adds the abbreviation for Eastern to the end

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: in signals the goddess sits inside another word
embrace shows the permitted word hugs the goddess between its letters

parts.note: OK means permitted or allowed
Kali is the Hindu goddess of time and destruction

explanation.surface: A worshipper glimpses Kali held in an approving hug, alongside an Eastern double.
explanation.definitionFit: A double who closely resembles someone is loosely called their twin, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sick aunt starts to recover without medical assistance

indicators.note: sick suggests something disordered, so the letters of aunt are rearranged

parts.note: fodder as written
to rally is to recover, as a patient rallies

explanation.surface: An ill aunt begins to get better without seeing a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick' rearranges AUNT as NATU; 'starts to' is a link meaning she begins to RALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something naturally, as in giving birth, means without drugs or medical intervention.

clue.text: Not happy about husband going to fish

indicators.note: about means the sad word goes around the letter

parts.note: sad means not happy

explanation.surface: An unhappy husband goes off fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The shad is a herring-like fish that swims upriver to spawn.

clue.text: Pregnant, so not working

definitions.meaning: a slang phrase for being with child
the same phrase means broken or ruined, of a machine or plan

explanation.walkthrough: The British slang phrase means both pregnant and broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang idiom has both senses: expecting a baby, and out of order or ruined.

clue.text: Run through poem, getting a line on very hard test

indicators.note: through means the run letter goes into the middle of the poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
r is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A poet works through a poem, adding a line under exam pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' puts R inside ODE to make ORDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful trial; medieval trial by ordeal was literally a test of guilt.

clue.text: Monster foreign tea said to be eaten by youngster

indicators.note: to be eaten by means the tea word goes inside the youngster word

parts.note: a minor is someone under the age of majority
the Greek letter tau corresponds to our letter whose name is said like tea

explanation.surface: A monstrous child swallows some foreign tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' works on the letter name: our letter said 'tea' has a Greek counterpart. 'to be eaten by' puts it inside the youngster word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan Minotaur was a man-eating creature with a bull's head and a man's body.

clue.text: Option at toss leads to sharp initial advantage

parts.note: when a coin is tossed you call heads or tails
tart means sharp-tasting, sour

explanation.surface: Calling correctly at the coin toss gives a team the first move.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is a lead given at the beginning of a race or contest.

clue.text: Courage captain's spoken of admiral

indicators.note: spoken of means we use the sound of the captain's name, not its spelling

parts.note: Captain Thomas Hardy commanded Nelson's flagship Victory at Trafalgar
Samuel Hood was an 18th-century British admiral

explanation.surface: A captain is praised for his bravery in talking about his admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken of' turns HARDY into HARDI by sound. Hardy was Nelson's flag captain ('Kiss me, Hardy'); Hood is a famous naval name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is boldness or daring, a dated synonym for bravery.

clue.text: Editors' resistance overcome byja poet

indicators.note: overcome by means the resistance letter is engulfed by the poet's name

parts.note: Robert Bridges was Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Editors find their opposition swept aside by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome by' engulfs R in the poet's name, after 'a'; the print's 'byja' is a typo for 'by a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who abridge, shortening texts, are editors; the apostrophe makes the clue plural possessive to match the plural answer.

clue.text: Thus old magistrate's assistant accepts one court officer

parts.note: so means thus or in this way

indicators.note: accepts means the assistant word takes in the letter for one

parts.note: a lictor attended a Roman magistrate, carrying the fasces
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old magistrate's aide takes on an officer of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts I inside LICTOR to make LICITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer who prepares cases and advises clients is an officer of the court in English law.

clue.text: Rooms fitted with concealed drawers, perhaps

indicators.note: with concealed means the fitted word hides the drawers inside it

parts.note: apt means fitted or suitable
those who draw are artists, art men

explanation.surface: A set of rooms with built-in furniture, its chests of drawers hidden from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' looks like furniture but means people who draw, ART MEN; 'with concealed' puts them inside APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms, called an apartment.

clue.text: Enchanting islander rejected foreign money, accepting English

indicators.note: rejected means the whole result is turned back to front
accepting means the currency word takes in the abbreviation for English

parts.note: the lira was the currency of Italy

explanation.surface: A magical islander refuses foreign currency unless it is English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts E into LIRA to make LEIRA; 'rejected' turns it around. Ariel is the spirit in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the spirit of Prospero's island in The Tempest, who works enchantments for him.

clue.text: Sort of dean Cobbett saw on his rides?

definitions.meaning: a church dean overseeing a group of country parishes
William Cobbett wrote ... Rides about touring the English countryside

explanation.walkthrough: Cobbett's book Rural Rides (1830) describes his horseback tours of English farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dean heads a deanery of parishes, and Cobbett's Rural Rides records the countryside.

clue.text: As Holmes regarded Moriarty — time for the Last Bow?

indicators.note: for the Last places the time word at the end, after the bow word

parts.note: a bow is an arch shape
time is called the enemy, as in time the old enemy

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes's nemesis faces him at the end, in the story His Last Bow.
explanation.walkthrough: His Last Bow is a Holmes story title, so 'Last Bow' looks like one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Moriarty was Holmes's chief foe, his supreme adversary.

clue.text: Popular nightclub potential scene of violence?

definitions.meaning: a lively and fashionable place of entertainment
a trouble zone where fighting may break out

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means both a fashionable venue and a trouble zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names both a lively venue and a region of likely conflict.

clue.text: Heartless negligence, fitting a part of battery for car

indicators.note: fitting means the battery part slots inside the other letters
heartless removes everything but the first and last letters of negligence

parts.note: a cell is one unit of a battery

explanation.surface: Careless work and fitting the wrong battery part spoil a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' keeps only the outer letters of 'negligence'; 'fitting' slots 'a' plus the battery unit between them. A balloon's car is its gondola.
explanation.definitionFit: The car of a balloon or airship, the passenger basket or cabin, is also called a nacelle.

clue.text: Medley gleeman arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of gleeman are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A minstrel arranges a medley of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: A gleeman was a medieval minstrel, which suits the music picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words, one borrowed from French, mean a jumble or assortment of varied things.

clue.text: I acted in awful show

indicators.note: awful means badly done, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: fodder as written
fodder as written

explanation.surface: An actor confesses to a part in a dreadful production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is fodder: the eight letters of I ACTED IN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to show or point it out.

clue.text: Compete for possession of equipment

definitions.meaning: in football, to try to win the ball from an opponent

explanation.walkthrough: In football or rugby you challenge for the ball; fishing gear is also called this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a challenge for the ball in sport and gear such as fishing rods.

clue.text: Into action without restraint

definitions.meaning: First World War soldiers went out of the trenches into battle this way

explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers climbed out of the trenches 'over the top' to attack; the phrase now also means excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the trench-war charge into battle and an idiom for excessive behaviour.

clue.text: Offer perhaps pounds to gain objective

parts.note: L stands for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: Perhaps propose some money as a way to achieve a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone something temporarily is one way of offering it, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Individual record set by network

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a rete is an anatomical network of vessels or nerves

explanation.surface: A single record gets put out by a broadcasting network.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate or distinct, each item individual.

clue.text: Hesitate to get loudspeaker short of watts

indicators.note: short of means the speaker word goes without the letter for watts

parts.note: a tweeter is a small loudspeaker for high frequencies
W is the symbol for watts

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over buying a speaker of too low a wattage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes W from TWEETER.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to waver or hesitate, as if wobbling on the brink.
